subject: Maths
title: Multiplying and dividing surds
subtitle: Surds · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can multiply and divide surds using the rules of surds.

key_vocab.definition: To multiply surds: √a × √b = √(ab). To divide surds: √a ÷ √b = √(a/b).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can multiply and divide surds using the rules of surds.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: multiply surds -- To multiply surds: √a × √b = √(ab). To divide surds: √a ÷ √b = √(a/b).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply or divide the numbers under the root sign. Multiply coefficients separately.
√a × √b = √(a × b)
Same rule works for division: √a ÷ √b = √(a ÷ b)

Key examples:
  ✓ √3 × √5 = √15  (multiply under the root)
  ✓ √6 × √6 = 6  (square root times itself = integer)
  ✓ √20 ÷ √5 = √4 = 2  (divide under the root)
  ✗ √3 × √5 = √8  (multiply, not add)
  ✗ 2√3 × 4√5 = 6√15  (should be 8√15)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – multiplying simple surds
  Calculate √3 × √7.
  Multiply under the root: 3 × 7 = 21
  √3 × √7 = √21
  √21 cannot be simplified
  √21
  (Multiply the radicands together.)

Example 2 – with coefficients
  Calculate 3√2 × 4√5.
  Multiply coefficients: 3 × 4 = 12
  Multiply surds: √2 × √5 = √10
  = 12√10
  12√10
  (Coefficients multiply separately from the surds.)
